page.description: SerenityOS editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A love letter to '90s user interfaces with a custom Unix-like core. A graphical Unix-like operating system for desktop computers built from scratch, featuring a modern 64-bit kernel with pre-emptive multi-threading.
pros: Built entirely from scratch – no inherited code
Modern 64-bit kernel with full POSIX compatibility
Hundreds of ports of popular open-source software available
Active Discord community and regular YouTube development updates
cons: No pre-built ISO or image files are distributed – project is build-from-source only
GitHub repository has no releases or tags; no nightly builds found
Requires compiling the entire system from source code (several hours on typical hardware)
Build-from-source project with no published images or release tags, so this page lists no images.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for SerenityOS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Pre-built images not available. The project requires building from source: clone the GitHub repository, follow the Build Instructions in the README, and compile the entire system. No installer or disk image is distributed.
